Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.p2p

Class NoiseXXHandshake

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.p2p.NoiseXXHandshake
public final class NoiseXXHandshake extends Object
A Noise-XX-style handshake: three messages that mutually authenticate two long-term X25519 identities and agree a pair of forward-secret, direction-separated AES-256-GCM keys, with no third-party dependency. The pattern is 
   -> e
   <- e, ee, s, es
   -> s, se
which gives mutual authentication (both static keys are exchanged and bound into the transcript) and forward secrecy (the session keys come from fresh ephemeral X25519 keypairs that are discarded afterwards). The transcript hash h binds every handshake byte, so a man-in-the-middle who substitutes a static key produces a different handshake hash and a different peer fingerprint - the basis of the app's TOFU pinning (TrustDecision).

The class is a pure state machine: it turns handshake messages in and out and derives keys, but never touches a socket. The caller (SecureChannel) writes each writeMessage(byte[]) result to the wire and feeds each received blob to readMessage(byte[]). Because the steps are explicit, the whole handshake is unit-testable headless and the two halves can even be driven against each other in one JVM.

Instances are not thread-safe; a single connecting thread drives one handshake to completion. Handshake payloads are optional: the first message has no cipher key yet, so per the Noise specification a message-1 payload would travel in the clear - the transport therefore exchanges identity and presence in encrypted frames after the handshake and passes empty payloads here.

The AEAD, KDF and DH primitives are exactly those of P2pCrypto; the cipher-key schedule uses a zero nonce because each handshake key is used for a single seal/open, and the running transcript hash is passed as additional authenticated data so every handshake ciphertext is bound to its position in the exchange.

  • Constructor Details

    • NoiseXXHandshake

      public NoiseXXHandshake(NoiseXXHandshake.Role role, KeyPair localStatic, byte[] prologue, SecureRandom random) throws GeneralSecurityException
      Begins a handshake.
      Parameters:
      role - which side to play
      localStatic - our long-term static X25519 identity keypair
      prologue - optional context both sides must agree on (may be null); it is hashed into the transcript so a mismatch fails the handshake
      random - the randomness source for the ephemeral keypair (a SecureRandom; a seeded one makes tests deterministic)
      Throws:
      GeneralSecurityException - if the initial hash cannot be computed
